prompt: In debian-cloud/debian-12, what is debian-cloud?
hint: Images belong to something, like every resource.

choices.text: The zone the image is stored in
choices.why: Images are global; the name before the slash is not a zone.

choices.text: The organisation that owns your project
choices.why: Your organisation has nothing to do with Debian's images.

choices.text: The public project that holds the image
choices.why: Right. Public images live in projects that exist only to hold them.

choices.text: A registry of container images
choices.why: These are disk images; containers come in lesson 21.

prompt: The same e2-standard-2 costs more per hour with Windows on it than with Debian. Why?
hint: Which images are in windows-cloud, rhel-cloud and suse-cloud?

choices.text: A licence fee is added per hour while the machine runs
choices.why: Right. Red Hat, SUSE and Windows carry one; free distributions do not.

choices.text: Windows needs a larger boot disk, and the disk is what costs more
choices.why: A larger disk adds a little, but the hourly difference is a licence.

choices.text: Windows machines are moved to a dearer series automatically
choices.why: The machine type stays what you chose.

choices.text: Google charges more for any image that is not its own
choices.why: Debian is not Google's and costs nothing extra.

prompt: A plan with data "google_compute_image" fails in the lab after a few minutes, while the same machine with image = "debian-cloud/debian-12" plans at once. Why?
hint: When is each one resolved?

choices.text: The family debian-12 has been deprecated by Debian
choices.why: The error was a name that could not be looked up, not a deprecation.

choices.text: Data sources are not supported by the google provider
choices.why: google_compute_image is one; it failed for want of the network.

choices.text: The token no-account is only accepted for strings
choices.why: No request reached anything that could accept or refuse a token.

choices.text: A data source is read during the plan, so it needs the API; a string is resolved at creation
choices.why: Right. The string is passed through, and Compute Engine resolves it later.

prompt: A pointer to the newest image of a line that has not been retired is called an image ___.
hint: debian-12 is one.

prompt: Once the team has an account, why does the lesson prefer the data source over the string for plans that people review?
hint: What does each one show in the plan?

choices.text: The data source makes the image cheaper to store
choices.why: Storage is the publisher's; a public image costs you nothing to reference.

choices.text: The plan then names the dated image a reviewer will boot
choices.why: Right. The string only says which family, and the family can move.

choices.text: The string form is deprecated in the google provider 8.9.0
choices.why: It planned without a warning in this very lesson.

choices.text: A data source stops the family from ever changing
choices.why: It reads where the family points now; it does not freeze it.

prompt: Order the deprecation states from the one a family can point to, to the one furthest from use.
hint: Active is usable; deleted is marked for removal.
trap: DELETED is a label too: it does not remove the image, and storage is billed until somebody deletes it.

prompt: Friday's build shop-web-v3 breaks the shop. What makes every new machine boot Thursday's v2 again, without editing a template that names the family?
hint: What does the family read?

choices.text: Deleting the family shop-web and creating it again
choices.why: A family is not a separate object to delete; it is a label on images.

choices.text: Renaming shop-web-v2 to shop-web-v4
choices.why: Images cannot be renamed, and the family reads state and age, not the number.

choices.text: Marking shop-web-v3 as DEPRECATED
choices.why: Right. The family skips it and points back at v2.

choices.text: Setting v2's state to ACTIVE, since it is already the newest
choices.why: v3 is the newest; v2 is already active and is passed over until v3 is deprecated.

prompt: Where does the lesson advise pinning a dated image name instead of following the family?
hint: Where must two machines be alike?

choices.text: In a managed group, where machines must match
choices.why: Right. And wherever an incident report must say exactly what ran.

choices.text: In development, so new patches arrive on time
choices.why: That is where following the family is advised.

choices.text: On a builder machine that will be deleted within the hour
choices.why: A builder's life is short; pinning it gains little.

choices.text: Wherever the image is a public one
choices.why: Public or not is not the question; sameness is.

prompt: Marking an image DELETED does not remove it: its ___ keeps being billed until somebody deletes it.
hint: What does an image cost while it exists?

prompt: Why bake the shop's runtime into an image instead of installing it at every boot?
hint: What changes from one boot to the next?

choices.text: Images are cheaper to store than packages are to download
choices.why: Price is not the argument; speed and sameness are.

choices.text: Startup scripts are not allowed on E2 machines
choices.why: They are allowed everywhere; lesson 7 uses one.

choices.text: A machine made from a public image cannot install packages
choices.why: It can; it is just slower and less predictable.

choices.text: Every boot is then fast and alike
choices.why: Right. The installation runs once, when the image is built.

prompt: The plan for google_compute_image showed source_disk as (known after apply). Why?
hint: Does the builder's disk exist yet?

choices.text: The provider hides disk names from plans for security
choices.why: Nothing is hidden; the value is unknown.

choices.text: The disk does not exist until the builder is created, so it has no name yet
choices.why: Right. That is the honest answer for a value that depends on another resource.

choices.text: The image would be made from a snapshot instead
choices.why: The file names the builder's boot disk as the source.

choices.text: No account is configured, so names are masked
choices.why: With an account the plan would show the same thing.

prompt: The image-build file creates a builder and an image of its disk. What step does Terraform not express, and why does it matter?
hint: What state should the disk be in when it is copied?

choices.text: Deleting the image after use, or its storage is billed
choices.why: Deleting is a separate concern; the missing step comes before the copy.

choices.text: Choosing storage_locations, which the file leaves out
choices.why: The file sets it to southamerica-east1.

choices.text: Stopping the builder first, so the disk is quiet
choices.why: Right. Terraform has no stop-then-copy step; gcloud after a stop, or Packer, does it.

choices.text: Putting the image in a family, which the file cannot do
choices.why: family = "shop-web" is in the file.

prompt: A 10 GiB image is built every night and never deleted. At 0.05 USD per GiB-month, what is the storage bill for the month after a year of builds (365 images)?
hint: 365 images, 10 GiB each, 0.05 each GiB.

prompt: Match each object to what it is for.
hint: One makes many alike; one puts one machine back.

pairs.right: A template disk for making many machines alike
One whole machine, its configuration and every disk
A copy of one disk at one moment, lesson 3
A pointer to the newest image not deprecated

right_distractors: A container image in a registry

prompt: What does image_name = "shop-web-{{timestamp}}" with image_family = "shop-web" give the team in Packer?
hint: Two builds, two names, one family.

choices.text: A unique name per build, each the family's newest
choices.why: Right. Each build moves the family's pointer forward.

choices.text: A build that overwrites the previous image in place
choices.why: Images are never overwritten; each build is a new one.

choices.text: An image that Google deletes after the timestamp passes
choices.why: Nothing is deleted automatically; that is the pipeline's job.

choices.text: A Terraform state entry per build
choices.why: Packer keeps no Terraform state.

prompt: What does g2-standard-4 carry that n1-standard-4 does not?
hint: An accelerator-optimised type.

choices.text: A local SSD
choices.why: That would be a -lssd suffix.

choices.text: Twice the vCPUs and twice the memory
choices.why: Both have four.

choices.text: An Arm processor
choices.why: Arm is the a in c4a.

choices.text: One NVIDIA L4 GPU
choices.why: Right. The GPU is part of the type.

prompt: Why must a GPU machine set on_host_maintenance = "TERMINATE"?
hint: What does live migration move, and what can it not?

choices.text: GPU machines are billed per maintenance event
choices.why: There is no such charge.

choices.text: The card is in one host and its memory cannot move with the machine
choices.why: Right. So the machine stops for maintenance instead of migrating.

choices.text: Terraform refuses MIGRATE for any N1 machine
choices.why: The plan accepts either; Compute Engine refuses at creation.

choices.text: TERMINATE makes the GPU faster by skipping the hypervisor
choices.why: It is about maintenance, not speed.

prompt: g2-standard-4 is 515.99 USD a month and e2-standard-2 is 48.92. How many times dearer is the GPU machine, to one decimal?
hint: Divide one by the other.

prompt: A team needs a T4 machine in southamerica-east1-a next Monday for a demo. What should they do first, this week?
hint: Two things can refuse the machine before the price matters.

choices.text: Write the Terraform and run a plan, which checks both
choices.why: A plan checks neither the zone's accelerators nor the quota.

choices.text: Switch to a g2-standard-4, which needs no quota
choices.why: G2 carries a GPU and needs GPU quota too.

choices.text: Check the zone has a T4 and request GPU quota
choices.why: Right. Quota is reviewed by Google and takes days, not minutes.

choices.text: Buy a committed use discount for the GPU
choices.why: A discount lowers a price; it does not make a GPU available.

prompt: On an N1 machine, Terraform attaches a GPU with a ___ block.
hint: Two words joined by an underscore.

prompt: Which machine is the one most worth stopping when it is idle, by the sheet?
hint: Look at the month column.

choices.text: g2-standard-4, at about 516 dollars a month
choices.why: Right. Ten times the e2-standard-2, paid whether or not the GPU works.

choices.text: e2-standard-2, because it has the most machines in a group
choices.why: Its month is about 49 dollars.

choices.text: c4a-standard-2, because Arm idles badly
choices.why: Idle Arm machines cost what the sheet says, about 66 dollars.

choices.text: e2-micro, because it is shared
choices.why: It is the cheapest on the sheet.

prompt: Put the steps of releasing a new shop-web image in order.
hint: Test before you trust it; roll back if it fails.
items: Build the image with Packer into the family shop-web
Create a test machine from the family
Check the shop works on it
If it fails, mark the new image DEPRECATED
trap: Deprecating comes last because it is the response to a failed test, not a step of every release.

prompt: Which of these does this lab let you see without an account? Choose all that apply.
hint: Local help and local plans work; questions to Google do not.

choices.text: The deprecation states, in gcloud's help
choices.why: Right; help is rendered on your computer.

choices.text: Which image debian-12 points to today
choices.why: That needs the data source, which needs the API.

choices.text: A plan for a GPU machine
choices.why: Right; it planned with guest_accelerator and TERMINATE.

choices.text: Which zones offer the NVIDIA T4
choices.why: accelerator-types list is a remote command.

prompt: A g2-standard-4 (0.706832276 USD an hour) is stopped every night and weekend, running 50 hours a week. What does it cost for 4 weeks, to the cent?
hint: 200 hours at the hourly price.

prompt: A group of web machines follows the family shop-web. A new build is published at noon and two machines are added at 13:00 by autoscaling. What is true?
hint: When is a family resolved?

choices.text: All machines switch to the new build at noon
choices.why: Running disks are not rewritten by a family moving.

choices.text: The new machines fail, because a family cannot change during the day
choices.why: A family can move at any time.

choices.text: Nothing changes until the template is planned again
choices.why: A family string is resolved at each creation, not at plan time.

choices.text: The two new machines run the new build and the others the old one
choices.why: Right. That is why a group pins its image, as lesson 4 shows.
